prerequisites: Knowledge of the physical principles of Mechanics.
Kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies.
Statics, centers of gravity and moments of inertia.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental transformations of motion performed by different types of mechanisms.
Know the fundamentals of mechanism analysis. Solve problems of position, trajectory, kinematic and dynamic analysis of planar mechanisms.
Establish kinematic relationships and operating conditions of gears and gear trains. Properly approach the design of cam-follower systems.
Perform static and dynamic balancing of rotating elements.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and concise presentation.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for teamwork and ability to develop multidisciplinary projects.
Knowledge of the principles of machine and mechanism theory.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to mechanisms. Bars, pairs, kinematic chains and mechanisms. Inversion of a mechanism. Degrees of freedom of a mechanism: Kutzbach's criterion.
Position analysis of planar mechanisms. Closure equation. Resolution using complex algebra (Raven's method). Applications: four-bar mechanisms, crank-slider mechanisms.

Kinematic analysis of planar mechanisms. Instantaneous centers of rotation. Analytical determination of velocities and accelerations. Raven's method (complex algebra). Chace's method (vector algebra).
Dynamic analysis of planar mechanisms. Newton-Euler resolution method. Applications: forces and moments in four-bar and crank-slider mechanisms.
Synthesis of mechanisms. Function, path and motion generation. Graphical synthesis. Analytical synthesis.
Gears and gear trains. Spur gears. Fundamental law of gearing. The involute profile of teeth. Other types of gears. Gear trains.
Balancing. Causes and effects of imbalance. Static balancing. Dynamic balancing.
Introduction to cam design. Classification of cams and followers. Standard cam movements. Polynomial cam design. Graphical cam profile design. Analytical cam design.
Knowledge and study of different mechanism models.
Position analysis of a four-bar mechanism. Determination of limit positions.
Position analysis of a crank-slider mechanism.
Kinematic analysis of a Whitworth mechanism. Instantaneous Centers of Rotation.
Design and Simulation of a gearbox.
teaching_methods: Guided practical activities (led by the teacher)

assessment_methods.method: Written exams of general knowledge and problem solving

assessment_rules: The percentage corresponding to continuous assessment grades will be applied from a minimum score of 5 in the final evaluations. Assignments and practical reports must be completed and submitted by the student on time according to the deadlines established throughout the course. Evaluation criteria will be announced in advance.
